q: You have uploaded a 40-page report. Which approach gets the most out of it?
options: Ask for one summary and stop there
Interrogate it: summary, key decisions, deadlines, action items, then follow-ups like you would ask a colleague
Read it page by page first, then ask your questions
Ask only yes-or-no questions to keep answers short
explanation: You do not read the document — you interrogate it. Ask for the summary, decisions, deadlines and action items, then follow up on whatever matters most, as you would with a colleague who has read it.

q: AI makes a claim from your document and you want to check it. What should you ask?
options: 'Which page or section does that claim come from?' — then check the ones that matter
'Is this definitely true?' — and trust the answer
Nothing, because AI never misreads or invents
Ask a second AI the same question and average the replies
explanation: AI can misread, skip or invent, so the Day 1 rule still applies: ask for sources — which page or section — and check the claims that matter. That habit is what keeps research safe.

q: What is the goal state for any document you are handed at work?
options: A full rewrite of the document in your own words
A one-page brief — summary, key points, action items, open questions — in minutes
A list of every fact the document contains
A second opinion from a different tool
explanation: The goal state is a one-page brief: summary, key points, action items and open questions, produced in minutes. Master that and you become the person everyone sends the hard documents to.
